item.research_question: Can a reduced-activation WxTaTiVCr high-entropy alloy and its W-rich derivatives be fabricated via elemental powder mixing and spark plasma sintering to achieve enhanced hardness and strength for fusion plasma-facing applications?
item.material_system: WxTaTiVCr high-entropy alloys with W content ranging from 32 to 90 at.% (nominal 30-90 at.%), containing in-situ TiC; specific samples denoted as 32 Ws to 90 Ws.
item.processing_route: Elemental powders (W, Ta, Ti, V, Cr) mixed via Turbula shaker (30 rpm, 3 hours); consolidated via spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 1600 °C, 50 MPa axial pressure, 100 °C/min heating rate, 10 minutes dwell time, under vacuum (10⁻³ torr) in graphite molds.
item.test_conditions: Micro-Vickers hardness test (1 kg load, 10 s dwell); room-temperature compression test (strain rate 10⁻³/s); XRD, SEM-EDS, TEM, EPMA, and ICP-OES characterization.
key_findings: Hardness increased to ~790 Hv for the 42 Ws sample, which is more than twofold higher than pure tungsten (~350 Hv).
Compressive yield strength increased to ~2200 MPa for the 32 Ws sample, approximately twice that of pure tungsten.
In-situ TiC formation was confirmed with a volume fraction varying from 1.1% to 8.5% and irregular sizes between 10 to 25 µm.
C15 cubic Laves phases formed in V- and Cr-rich regions in samples with W content exceeding 70 at.% (71 Ws, 77 Ws, 90 Ws).
Relative density increased as W content decreased, with the 32 Ws sample showing the highest density due to liquid-phase assisted sintering.
Grain sizes were ~30–50 µm for samples with 32–63 at.% W (liquid-phase sintering) and ~3 µm for samples with 71–90 at.% W (solid-state sintering).
The BCC crystal structure was confirmed for the HEA matrix with a lattice parameter of 0.317 nm, while TiC exhibited an FCC structure with a lattice parameter of 0.43 nm.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the enhanced hardness and strength primarily to solid-solution strengthening caused by differences in atomic radii of the constituents, which hinders dislocation movement, and dispersion strengthening provided by the in-situ TiC particles. Additionally, grain boundary strengthening from TiC and the Hall-Petch effect from smaller grain sizes in high-W alloys contribute to the mechanical properties.
item.limitations: The study notes that while the chemical composition meets reduced-activation criteria, the actual reduced-activation behavior, irradiation resistance, hydrogen retention, and high-temperature mechanical properties have not yet been analyzed and require future investigation.
item.future_work: The authors propose that analysis of reduced-activation behavior, irradiation resistance, hydrogen retention, and high-temperature mechanical properties is necessary prior to utilizing the material as an armor material in future fusion reactors like DEMO.
quotes: A mechanical examination of the samples revealed a more than twofold improvement in the hardness and strength due to solid-solution strengthening and dispersion strengthening.
The increased hardness is attributed to differences in the atomic radii of the constituents of the high-entropy alloy (x = 32).
The C15 Laves phase has cubic symmetry, a structure similar to that of MgCu2, and contains two sublattices.
